title: Diagonal language outside a time class
statement: Let $g,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfy the condition that for every $A,N\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $n\ge N$ such that $A\bigl(T(n)+n+1\bigr)^2\le g(n)$. Then the language of binary strings $x$ for which the diagonal simulator does not halt with output $1$ after exactly $g(|x|)$ steps does not belong to $\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $A,N\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists $n\ge N$ with $A(T(n)+n+1)^2\le g(n)$
replaced:
Let $g,T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy the following growth condition: for every
$A,N \in \mathbb{N}$, there is some $n \ge N$ such that $A(T(n)+n+1)^2 \le g(n)$. Then
the language of binary strings on which the fixed diagonal machine does not output the
single bit $1$ within $g(n)$ steps, where $n$ is the string length, does not belong to
$\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$; that is, no constant-factor time bound $cT(n)$ suffices for a
machine deciding it.
